【原视频简介】
I made iron using the old blower variant but using a larger diameter fan (30 cm rather than 25 cm). I did a longer smelt and a shorter smelt. The long smelt made 10 g of iron but the short smelt made 14 g sugesting that multiple shorter duration smelts may be more effective at producing iron rather than one long smelt. The iron was then put into a knife shaped mold and placed in a forge under a flattened tuyere to spread the blast ino a sheet. The iron in the mold partially welded and fused but didn't completely melt and it was broken in the middle. I put this down to the mold being too far under the tuyere blast as the coals above got white hot. I'm counting this as a partial sucess because the result could still be sharpened into some type of tool. The iron knife I made previously this was melted much more completely in its mold and further exeperimentation would be needed to re-learn this method of insitu casting.

#primitivetechnology #iron #handmade #engineering 

The ultimate challenge is seeing how far human ingenuity can go. Subscribe here:
https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCAL3JXZSzSm8AlZyD3nQdBA?sub_confirmation=1

About Primitive Technology:
Building things in the wild completely from scratch no modern tools, no modern materials.
The challenge is simple but strict: If I need a fire, I make a fire stick. If I need an axe, I shape a stone. Every hut is built solely from trees, mud, and rocks. I don't live in the wild, but I love discovering just how far we can go using only natural materials…
